arms.run:
set -uo pipefail

# WHY THIS ARM EXISTS, and why it runs on THIS runner and not a Mac.
# `mktemp -t NAME` with a template carrying fewer than three consecutive X is a
# BSD/macOS-only form. GNU coreutils — this ubuntu runner — refuses it:
#     mktemp: too few X's in template 'NAME'
# The LOUD sites red their arm. The SILENT ones do not: a failing command
# substitution inside an assignment does NOT trip `set -e`, so the variable
# becomes the EMPTY string and the script runs on, redirecting into "".
# scripts/pds-personal-local-smoke_test.sh did exactly that — run 35435212884
# printed `0 of  doc anchor(s) resolved` and its leg still reported SUCCESS.
# A guard whose own home is a Mac would never have seen it.

echo "── 1. the guard proves it can SEE (positive control) ──"
bash scripts/mktemp-portability-check.sh --selftest

echo "── 2. the guard over the tracked tree ──"
bash scripts/mktemp-portability-check.sh

# 3. THE ORIGINAL VACUOUS GREEN, asserted by its NUMBER and not by an exit code.
# The regression's signature was a PASSING run that measured nothing, so the
# only honest assertion is that the count is non-zero.
echo "── 3. personal-local --dry-run resolves a NON-ZERO number of doc anchors ──"
out="$(bash scripts/pds-personal-local-smoke_test.sh --dry-run 2>&1)" || {
  printf '%s\n' "$out"
  echo "RED: pds-personal-local-smoke_test.sh --dry-run exited non-zero" >&2
  exit 1
}
printf '%s\n' "$out" | grep -E 'doc anchor\(s\) resolved' || {
  printf '%s\n' "$out"
  echo "RED: the run printed no doc-anchor tally at all" >&2
  exit 1
}
n="$(printf '%s\n' "$out" | sed -n 's/^ *\([0-9][0-9]*\) of \([0-9][0-9]*\) doc anchor(s) resolved.*/\1/p' | tail -1)"
tot="$(printf '%s\n' "$out" | sed -n 's/^ *\([0-9][0-9]*\) of \([0-9][0-9]*\) doc anchor(s) resolved.*/\2/p' | tail -1)"
[ -n "${n:-}" ] && [ -n "${tot:-}" ] || {
  echo "RED: could not parse the tally; a 0-of-EMPTY denominator is exactly the bug" >&2
  exit 1
}
echo "  parsed: $n of $tot doc anchor(s) resolved"
[ "$tot" -gt 0 ] || { echo "RED: denominator is 0 — the plan file was never written" >&2; exit 1; }
[ "$n" -gt 0 ]   || { echo "RED: 0 anchors resolved — a green that measured nothing" >&2; exit 1; }

arms.name: stat portability guard — selftest (8 controls incl. a planted RED), tree scan, and the pds-artifact-retention arm tally asserted BY NUMBER
arms.run:
set -uo pipefail

# WHY THIS ARM EXISTS, and why only this runner can prove it.
# `-f` means OPPOSITE things in the two stats:
#     BSD / macOS    stat -f FORMAT path   "render path with this FORMAT"
#     GNU coreutils  stat -f path          "print FILE SYSTEM status" (format is -c)
# So the common defensive idiom, written BSD-first:
#     mtime="$(stat -f %m "$p" 2>/dev/null || stat -c %Y "$p")"
# does NOT skip the fallback. The first command POLLUTES STDOUT with a
# filesystem report and only then fails, so the fallback appends the RIGHT
# number to the WRONG text and every comparison downstream is against garbage.
# Nothing reports an error. Measured: run 35504059438 / job 106061128225 —
# scripts/pds-artifact-retention.test.sh was 24 passed / 11 FAILED on ubuntu
# while the identical tree was 35/0 on macOS.
#
# That harness could not run here AT ALL until #19419 (a GNU mktemp refusal
# killed it at startup, exit 99), so those eleven failures had never been seen.
# A guard whose own home is a Mac cannot see either defect.

echo "-- 1. the guard proves it can SEE (positive control) --"
bash scripts/stat-portability-check.sh --selftest

echo "-- 2. the guard over the tracked tree --"
bash scripts/stat-portability-check.sh

# 3. THE SUBJECT, asserted by its NUMBERS and not by an exit code.
# This regression's signature is a harness that runs and quietly measures the
# wrong thing, so the honest assertion names the pass and failure counts.
echo "-- 3. pds-artifact-retention.test.sh arm tally, asserted by number --"
out="$(bash scripts/pds-artifact-retention.test.sh 2>&1)" || {
  printf '%s\n' "$out"
  echo "RED: pds-artifact-retention.test.sh exited non-zero" >&2
  exit 1
}
printf '%s\n' "$out" | grep -E '[0-9]+ pass\(es\), [0-9]+ failure\(s\)' >/dev/null || {
  printf '%s\n' "$out"
  echo "RED: the run printed no arm tally at all -- it never reached its summary" >&2
  exit 1
}
p="$(printf '%s\n' "$out" | sed -n 's/^ *\([0-9][0-9]*\) pass(es), \([0-9][0-9]*\) failure(s).*/\1/p' | tail -1)"
f="$(printf '%s\n' "$out" | sed -n 's/^ *\([0-9][0-9]*\) pass(es), \([0-9][0-9]*\) failure(s).*/\2/p' | tail -1)"
[ -n "${p:-}" ] && [ -n "${f:-}" ] || {
  echo "RED: could not parse the tally; an EMPTY count is exactly this bug's shape" >&2
  exit 1
}
echo "  parsed: $p pass(es), $f failure(s)"
[ "$f" -eq 0 ] || { printf '%s\n' "$out"; echo "RED: $f arm(s) failed" >&2; exit 1; }
[ "$p" -gt 0 ] || { echo "RED: 0 arms passed -- a green that measured nothing" >&2; exit 1; }

arms.name: pds-citation-expand 4-arm harness (the guard's 16 selftest arms + its LIVE --check over the PDS fence)
pds-idle-sampler --selftest — 3 arms (killed-mid-window, clean cleanup, KEEP control); fake ssh on PATH, no host
PDS-D allocation arbiter: --check-alloc and --axis a, --axis d, --axis f over the merged tree
arms.run:
set -uo pipefail

CHARTER=.claude/workflows/bp-pds-charter.md
ALLOC=tooling/pds/d-number-reservations.tsv

for f in "$CHARTER" "$ALLOC"; do
  [ -f "$f" ] || { echo "RED: $f is missing from this tree -- the arbiter has nothing to compare" >&2; exit 1; }
done

# The definition lens, byte-for-byte charter_defined_numbers() from
# scripts/pds-record-parity.sh: bold-lead bullet UNION own-line heading.
# NOT "any PDS-D anywhere" -- the charter's prose names the synthetic
# fixtures PDS-D777/PDS-D999 and a looser lens would read them as a
# high-water mark of 999.
charter_hw=$( { grep -oE '^[[:space:]]*([-*][[:space:]]+)?\*\*PDS-D[0-9]+' "$CHARTER" || true
                grep -oE '^#+[[:space:]]+PDS-D[0-9]+([[:space:]]|$)' "$CHARTER" || true
              } | grep -oE 'PDS-D[0-9]+' | sed 's/^PDS-D//' | sort -n -u | tail -1 )
ledger_hw=$(awk -F'\t' '$1 ~ /^PDS-D[0-9]+$/ { sub(/^PDS-D/, "", $1); print $1 }' "$ALLOC" | sort -n -u | tail -1)
res_count=$(awk -F'\t' '$1 ~ /^PDS-D[0-9]+$/ { print $1 }' "$ALLOC" | sort -u | wc -l | tr -d ' ')
seed=$(awk -F'\t' '$1 == "SEED" { print $2; exit }' "$ALLOC")

echo "── the three counts this step compares (derived HERE, from this tree) ──"
echo "  charter high-water:  PDS-D${charter_hw:-<none>}   (highest number DEFINED in $CHARTER)"
echo "  ledger  high-water:  PDS-D${ledger_hw:-<none, only the SEED row>}   (highest number RESERVED in $ALLOC)"
echo "  reservations:        ${res_count} number(s) reserved above the seed"
echo "  seed:                ${seed:-<none>}   (at or below it predates the arbiter, not scored)"
[ -n "${charter_hw:-}" ] || { echo "RED: the charter defines no PDS-D at all -- the lens is measuring itself, not the corpus" >&2; exit 1; }

rc_total=0
# `--axis d` joins the loop: it is PURE-TREE like --check-alloc (charter
# + the PDS scripts, no network, no git walk), so it runs everywhere
# --axis a does and cannot go UNCHECKED on a shallow checkout.
#
# `--axis f` joins it too, and on a DIFFERENT warrant from d's, because it
# is NOT pure-tree: it walks every commit that has ever touched
# scripts/pds-pull-proof.sh and runs `git merge-base --is-ancestor`, so it
# needs the full graph. This leg declares "fetch_depth": 0, which is why it
# may run HERE and not wherever a shallow checkout is taken -- and if the
# graph is ever short, f returns rc 2 UNCHECKED, which the case below already
# scores RED rather than passing. It is offline (no curl, no bp, no http) and
# it ran 2.6s locally against this leg's 15-minute budget. Until now it ran in
# no job at all: a guard nothing executes is a guard that decays in silence.
for arm in --check-alloc "--axis a" "--axis d" "--axis f"; do
  echo "── bash scripts/pds-record-parity.sh $arm ──"
  # `|| rc=$?` and NOT a bare call followed by `rc=$?`: the default
  # shell for a `run:` block is `bash -e {0}`, which would exit on the
  # non-zero BEFORE the case below ever classified it -- the step would
  # still be red, but the log would never say DIVERGENT or UNCHECKED.
  rc=0
  # shellcheck disable=SC2086
  bash scripts/pds-record-parity.sh $arm || rc=$?
  case "$rc" in
    0) echo "  rc=0 PARITY" ;;
    1) echo "  rc=1 DIVERGENT -- RED. The charter, the reservation ledger and the commit corpus disagree; see above." >&2; rc_total=1 ;;
    2) echo "  rc=2 UNCHECKED -- RED, NOT A PASS. The arm could not look (truncated walk, missing charter, no SEED row)." >&2; rc_total=1 ;;
    3) echo "  rc=3 USAGE -- RED. This step invoked the script wrongly." >&2; rc_total=1 ;;
    *) echo "  rc=$rc UNKNOWN -- RED." >&2; rc_total=1 ;;
  esac
done
exit "$rc_total"

arms.run:
set -euo pipefail
f=.github/workflows/cloud.yml
call=$(grep -n 'migration-version-collision-check.sh' "$f" | cut -d: -f1 | sed -n '1p')
if [ -z "$call" ]; then
  echo "::error::$f no longer invokes scripts/migration-version-collision-check.sh"
  exit 1
fi
test_line=$(grep -n '^        run: mix test$' "$f" | cut -d: -f1 | sed -n '1p')
if [ -z "$test_line" ]; then
  echo "::error::$f has no 'run: mix test' step; this assertion cannot bind and refuses rather than passing"
  exit 1
fi
if [ "$call" -ge "$test_line" ]; then
  echo "::error::the collision check (line $call) runs at or AFTER mix test (line $test_line); a silent no-op would reach a green suite"
  exit 1
fi
echo "cloud.yml: collision check at line $call, mix test at line $test_line — ordered correctly"

arms.name: scratchpad-reaper.sh syntax check
scratchpad-reaper.test.sh syntax check
the reaper's skip gates can still LOSE (49 checks, 3 differential controls, mktemp git fixtures)
the free-space guard the reaper delegates its verdict to still bites
--floor refuses ON THIS RUNNER above its measured free space, and passes below it
arms.run:
# `set +e` is LOAD-BEARING and its absence failed this step on
# 2026-09-13: GitHub runs every `run:` body as `bash -e {0}`, so the
# deliberate non-zero REFUSAL below aborted the step before
# `rc_refuse=$?` could read it — the step reporting a failure for
# doing exactly what it was asserting. `set -uo pipefail` does not
# cancel an inherited -e.
set +e
set -uo pipefail
avail_gb=$(df -P -k . | awk 'NR==2 {print int($4/1024/1024)}')
case "$avail_gb" in
  ''|*[!0-9]*)
    echo "::error::CANNOT READ — df gave no GiB figure for the workspace; refusing to report a floor verdict it did not measure"
    exit 1 ;;
esac
above=$((avail_gb + 1000))
bash scripts/scratchpad-reaper.sh --floor "$above" .
rc_refuse=$?
bash scripts/scratchpad-reaper.sh --floor 0 .
rc_pass=$?
echo "measured: ${avail_gb} GiB free · floor ${above} GiB -> rc=${rc_refuse} · floor 0 GiB -> rc=${rc_pass}"
if [ "$rc_refuse" != "2" ]; then
  echo "::error::a floor above the measured free space returned $rc_refuse, not the REFUSED code 2"
  exit 1
fi
if [ "$rc_pass" != "0" ]; then
  echo "::error::a floor of 0 GiB returned $rc_pass, not OK"
  exit 1
fi
echo "the floor is distinguishable: REFUSED=2, OK=0, on the same path."
